statusDefinitions.end-to-end verified: Verified live in active developer session and automated protocol tests
statusDefinitions.protocol-tested: Standard MCP JSON-RPC protocol compliance and tool schema parity verified via StdioClientTransport
statusDefinitions.configured: Configuration schema and adapter templates provided; headless verification confirmed
statusDefinitions.implemented: Code interface implemented; awaiting host binary for live run
statusDefinitions.limited: Supported via CLI or partial extension interfaces due to host environment constraints
statusDefinitions.unverified: Configuration provided but host binary absent from test environment

clients.name: Google Antigravity
clients.integrationMechanism: MCP stdio + CLI workspace execution + Reusable Skills
accessibleFeatures: All 207 REA tools dynamically discoverable via forge_rea_discover or exposed via --mode full
CLI commands (forge capabilities, forge adapters, forge recreate, forge create, forge wasp, forge rea, forge doctor)
clients.testEvidence: Verified in active live Antigravity IDE workspace session. Both standalone CLI and spawned StdioClientTransport MCP client pass 100% of automated tests.
clients.limitations: Native Wasp CLI execution requires WSL when running inside Windows host workspaces.

clients.name: Claude Code / Claude Desktop
clients.testEvidence: Claude binary verified. Protocol tested with official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk client with zero stdout pollution.
clients.limitations: Desktop application cannot directly invoke interactive CLI prompts; communicates exclusively via MCP tool calls.

clients.name: Cursor
clients.integrationMechanism: Cursor Settings -> Features -> MCP Server (command transport) or .cursor/mcp.json
clients.testEvidence: Protocol compliance and tool registration confirmed via StdioClientTransport tests with 214 tools discovered.
clients.limitations: Cursor configuration merges into .cursor/mcp.json; automated adapter provides safe merging.

clients.name: OpenCode
clients.integrationMechanism: MCP stdio server and direct CLI execution
accessibleFeatures: Direct CLI execution ('forge capabilities', 'forge recreate', 'forge create', 'forge wasp', 'forge rea', 'forge doctor')
clients.testEvidence: OpenCode binary verified. CLI argument forwarding and exit code propagation verified in automated test suite.
clients.limitations: Requires Node.js >= 22.13.0 on host machine for native SQLite support.

clients.name: VS Code / GitHub Copilot
clients.integrationMechanism: VS Code Task / Extension Terminal execution + experimental MCP extension (.vscode/mcp.json)
accessibleFeatures: MCP tool suite when Copilot MCP extension is active
clients.testEvidence: VS Code CLI execution and task framing tested and verified with standard process spawning.
clients.limitations: Copilot Chat native MCP support requires compatible VS Code preview extension; CLI automation is the primary verified channel.

clients.name: Cline (VS Code Extension)
accessibleFeatures: Automated workspace synthesis and verifier loops
clients.testEvidence: Standard MCP JSON-RPC protocol compliance verified against SDK schema standards.
clients.limitations: File creation permissions depend on Cline's user-approval settings in the VS Code GUI.

clients.name: Roo Code (Roo Clinic)
clients.testEvidence: Verified compatible with standard MCP 1.6+ protocol schemas.
clients.limitations: Requires user approval for file overwriting outside active workspace.

clients.name: Windsurf (Codeium Cascade)
accessibleFeatures: Cascade tool invocation and contextual code generation
clients.testEvidence: Stdio protocol compliance verified via StdioClientTransport tests.
clients.limitations: Windsurf configuration automatically managed via 'forge adapters setup windsurf'.

clients.name: Gemini CLI
clients.integrationMechanism: Direct CLI execution + JSON output parsing
clients.testEvidence: CLI commands and subprocess JSON stdout parsing verified in test suite.
clients.limitations: Gemini CLI lacks native background stdio MCP daemon; relies on CLI execution.

clients.name: Codex CLI
clients.integrationMechanism: Direct CLI execution and script invocation
clients.testEvidence: Verified CLI exit codes, stdout framing, and error streams.
clients.limitations: Terminal execution requires non-interactive flags where supported.
